findings.description: F001 requires override evidence to be durably written but only pins this as flushed, leaving the crash-durability contract ambiguous for the override record and binding snapshot.
findings.recommendation: Define the durable-write standard before implementation, including whether file fsync, parent-directory fsync, atomic temp-file replacement, or append-only semantics are required, and add tests at that boundary.

findings.description: F002 blocks unregistered nested .git directories but does not pin the policy for registered submodules containing dirty, untracked, or ignored local state that git worktree removal may still delete.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit submodule rule: either recursively require registered submodules to be clean and ignored-free, or block removal whenever populated submodules are present until a separate audited cleanup exists.

findings.description: F002 specifies a post-destruction removal-OUTCOME audit entry but does not pin behavior if that outcome append fails after git worktree remove succeeds.
findings.recommendation: Require the command to exit non-zero, name the missing outcome audit, preserve the prior intent evidence, and define the rerun/status behavior for this partially completed state.

findings.description: F003 says the initial allowlist entry is environments_json, but the contract needs an exact repo-root-relative path so tests and implementation cannot diverge on the local config file name.
findings.recommendation: Pin the allowlist value as the literal repo-relative path, for example environments.json if that is intended, and make the test assert that exact path.
